neighbours.label: The 'that' or 'it' right after a sign, note, label or caption, where 'said' is expected next ('a sign that said…', 'under his picture it said…'); the same nouns without such a slot stay low.
fire: We passed a sign that said the bridge was closed.
On the box was a label that said fragile.
Below the photo it said he was born in 1920.
She found a note that said meet me at noon.
The banner over the door said welcome home.
On the wall was a poster that said no smoking.
At the bottom of the page it said draft.
He held a card that said thank you.
quiet: We passed a sign near the old bridge.
On the box was a red label.
Below the photo was a frame of oak.
She found a note under the door.
The banner over the door was faded.
On the wall was a poster of the band.
At the bottom of the page was a stain.
He held a card in his hand.

short: 'that/it' before 'said' for a sign or note
notes: Card: ' that' x7, ' It' x3, ' which' x3, ' report' x3 (The king's⟦ note⟧ said; a sign today⟦ that⟧ said; under his little picture⟦ it⟧ said); output promotes ' said', ' stated', ' mentioned'. Exploratory probe: 'a sign that said' 0.71, 'it said he had died' 0.42, 'the king's note said' 0.23, but 'the king's note was torn' 0.23 too; 'a sign near the road' 0.11.
